stem: Which of the following best states the main point of the passage?

choices.text: Ants are the most important seed-spreading animals in any forest.
Ants gain much of their food from the fatty appendages of wildflower seeds.
Seeds left in ant nests benefit more from the nest's safety and fertility than from being carried far from the parent plant.
Researchers have been wrong about every aspect of how ants affect wildflowers.
Wildflowers that depend on ants grow more slowly than those that do not.

explanation: The passage corrects an earlier assumption (distance) and ends by naming the real advantage: the safety and fertility of the nest site.

choiceExplanations.A: Too broad: the passage discusses woodland wildflowers only and makes no comparison with other animals.
choiceExplanations.B: A detail: the appendage is mentioned as the lure, but the passage never says how much of the ants' diet it supplies.
choiceExplanations.D: Too extreme: researchers were wrong about the chief benefit (distance), not about everything.
choiceExplanations.E: Not mentioned: growth rates are never discussed.

stem: Select the sentence that describes a way entrants try to overcome the difficulty.

answer.sentence: Entrants sometimes break the deadlock by subsidizing one side, usually buyers, in the expectation that the other side will follow.

explanation: The subsidy strategy is the only attempted solution described.

stem: Select the sentence that states the author's main conclusion.

answer.sentence: The greater advantage appears to be the safety and fertility of the nest site rather than the distance travelled.

explanation: The final sentence carries the author's conclusion; the earlier sentences describe the process, the old assumption and the measurements that overturn it.

stem: Which of the following best summarizes the passage?

choices.text: Although book lending has fallen, libraries are likely to endure by meeting other community needs.
Critics are right that falling book lending shows libraries have outlived their purpose.
Municipal budgets will soon shift to support the new role of libraries.
Job-search workshops are the main reason library attendance has grown.
Library attendance has grown because book lending has declined.

explanation: The author concedes the decline in lending, then points to rising attendance and predicts survival through a different role.

choiceExplanations.B: Reversed: the critics' view is reported and then answered with the attendance figures.
choiceExplanations.C: Contradicts the passage, which calls the adaptation of budgets 'far from certain'.
choiceExplanations.D: Too narrow and too strong: workshops are one of several drivers, and the passage never ranks them.
choiceExplanations.E: Confuses two separate trends; the passage does not say that one causes the other.

stem: Which of the following best expresses the main idea of the passage?

choices.text: Subsidizing buyers is the most effective strategy for any new platform.
Mutual reinforcement between buyers and sellers makes it hard for new marketplace platforms to enter.
Technically superior products usually defeat established platforms.
Platforms grow slowly because sellers distrust buyers.
Buyers value platforms more than sellers do.

explanation: The passage explains why growth is slow, why entrants struggle and how some try to break in.

choiceExplanations.A: Too strong: subsidy is costly and works 'only if' buyers stay.
choiceExplanations.C: Reversed: a superior product may still fail to attract users.
choiceExplanations.D: Slow initial growth is attributed to mutual dependence, not distrust.
choiceExplanations.E: Neither group is said to value platforms more.

stem: Which of the following best expresses the main idea of the passage?

choices.text: Adaptations should always change the plot of the original.
Novels are experienced so differently that no film can succeed as an adaptation.
Critics who value fidelity lack knowledge about film.
Irony is the most important quality of any novel.
Faithfulness in an adaptation is better measured by interpretive spirit than by reproduction of events.

explanation: The passage argues against fidelity of incident and for fidelity to the work's tone and concerns.

choiceExplanations.A: Too extreme: departures are legitimate only where they serve the work's central concern.
choiceExplanations.B: The passage claims adaptation is interpretation, not that it must fail.
choiceExplanations.C: The passage attacks a standard, not the critics' knowledge.
choiceExplanations.D: Irony is one example of a quality an adaptation might capture; no ranking is made.

stem: Consider each of the three answer choices separately and select all that apply. Which of the following does the author offer as support for the central claim?

choices.text: Singers rebuild each performance from stock phrases rather than memorizing it.
No two performances of an oral poem are identical.
Transcribers often alter the words they record in order to improve them.

explanation: A and B are the evidence for the claim that a transcript preserves just one occasion. C is not in the passage.

choiceExplanations.C: The passage never says transcribers change the words.

stem: Select the sentence that states a specific mechanism proposed by the newer work.

answer.sentence: Even simple molecules can remain for centuries if they cling to mineral grains or sit in pockets too small for microbes to enter.

explanation: This sentence says how carbon can persist: by clinging to mineral grains or being trapped in pockets too small for microbes. The sentence before it only announces that a different explanation exists.

stem: Consider each of the three answer choices separately and select all that apply. Which of the following does the author use to support the central claim?

choices.text: Readers experience the same novel in different ways.
A film can keep the plot of a novel yet lose its tone.
Most adaptations alter at least one major plot event.

explanation: A and B are offered as reasons why reproduction is the wrong standard. C is not stated anywhere.

choiceExplanations.C: The passage never says how common alterations are.

stem: Which of the following best states the central point of the passage?

choices.text: A written text of an oral epic captures one performance among many, so none should be treated as the definitive original.
Oral singers memorize their poems more reliably than is generally believed.
The great oral epics were each composed by a single gifted author.
Transcribed epics are unreliable because transcribers make mistakes.
Living oral traditions are more creative than written literature.

explanation: The passage argues that a recorded text is one sample of a variable tradition, and recommends seeing the epic as the whole family of performances.

choiceExplanations.B: Reversed: singers 'rarely memorize them word for word'.
choiceExplanations.C: The first sentence presents this as a tempting image the passage rejects.
choiceExplanations.D: Errors by transcribers are never mentioned.
choiceExplanations.E: No comparison between oral and written literature is made.

stem: The author mentions the decline in book lending primarily in order to

choices.text: show that libraries will not survive in their present form
suggest that attendance statistics are unreliable
argue that libraries should stop lending books altogether
grant a point made by critics before arguing that it does not settle the matter
demonstrate that the public no longer values reading

explanation: 'Indeed' concedes the fact, 'Some critics' attaches their inference, and 'But' turns to the evidence that leads away from their conclusion. The decline is support for a concession, not the main point.

choiceExplanations.A: The author does not predict the end of libraries; the argument is that they will survive differently.
choiceExplanations.B: The author uses the attendance figures, not casting doubt on them.
choiceExplanations.C: No recommendation about lending is made.
choiceExplanations.E: The decline in lending is reported; nothing is said about the public's valuation of reading.

stem: Which of the following best summarizes the passage?

choices.text: Soils store more carbon than the atmosphere and vegetation combined, which makes them the main cause of climate change.
Newer research suggests that carbon persists in soil largely because of soil structure and minerals rather than the carbon's own chemistry.
Complex molecules decay more slowly than simple molecules in all soils.
Farm practices cannot affect the amount of carbon stored in soil.
Microbes are unable to decompose carbon in any soil.

explanation: The passage contrasts an older view (chemistry) with a newer one (structure and minerals) and draws a consequence from the newer one.

choiceExplanations.A: The first sentence is background; the passage does not blame soils for climate change.
choiceExplanations.C: This is the older view that the passage reports and questions.
choiceExplanations.D: The passage says the practical consequences concern how to change storage, not that practices have no effect.
choiceExplanations.E: Microbes are blocked only where carbon is in tiny pockets or bound to minerals.
